name: Magna-Power Electronics
old_description: Robust power processing topologies combined with state-of-the-art vertically integrated USA manufacturing and worldwide support.
about:
Magna-Power Electronics was founded in 1981 in Flemington, New Jersey, where it maintains a vertically integrated manufacturing headquarters. The company designs and builds programmable DC power supplies and electronic loads, controlling the entire production process from sheet metal fabrication and machining to printed circuit board assembly and final test.

The facility houses CNC vertical and horizontal machining centers, wire EDM, robotic bonded-fin heat-sink assembly, SMT lines with a Europlacer stencil printer and IINEO pick-and-place, two through-hole insertion lines, and 14 assembly stations for wire harnessing and sub-assembly. Magna-Power reports more than 250,000 available configurations spanning 1.5 kW to 10,000 kW+, with over 475 MW of product shipped and 50,000 units delivered to date. Typical made-to-order build time is four to six weeks.

Customers range from startups to Fortune 500 companies across aerospace, defense, academic research, robotics, and energy sectors. Named references include GE Aviation, Lockheed Martin, QinetiQ, Blue Robotics, Alencon Systems, and universities such as the University of Houston, George Washington University, and Colorado School of Mines.

The company attributes its differentiation to vertical integration, which gives it control over quality, cost, and lead times, and to co-locating engineering with manufacturing to foster continuous improvement. A large inventory of common assemblies supports industry-leading made-to-order delivery, while unified firmware, SCPI commands, and standard options such as high slew rate, integrated blocking diode, water cooling, and the DBx module simplify integration across product families.
